upsert.title: Olaparib plus meloxicam for feline mammary carcinoma
upsert.center: University of Minnesota College of Veterinary Medicine
upsert.funding: Study covers screening, olaparib, meloxicam, required study visits, bloodwork and chest radiographs, plus a $2,000 credit toward tumor surgery and up to $1,000 toward treatment of study-medication complications at the University of Minnesota.
upsert.notes: Pilot PARP-inhibitor treatment study. No radiation, chemotherapy or other investigational drugs within 14 days before enrollment; additional protocol criteria apply.

upsert.title: CAR-neutrophils combined with radiation for canine glioma
upsert.center: UT Southwestern Veterinary Research and Oncology Clinic (VROC)
upsert.notes: Evaluates CAR-neutrophils plus radiation to induce tumor shrinkage and improve survival in dogs with glioma. Contact VROC for protocol-specific eligibility and costs.

upsert.title: Ferumoxytol combined with radiation therapy for canine glioma
upsert.center: UT Southwestern Veterinary Research and Oncology Clinic (VROC)
upsert.notes: Treatment study evaluating ferumoxytol plus radiation therapy in dogs with glioma.

upsert.title: Weekly intratumoral cowpea mosaic virus immunotherapy for canine solid tumors
upsert.center: UT Southwestern Veterinary Research and Oncology Clinic (VROC)
upsert.notes: Evaluates weekly intratumoral CPMV as an immunotherapy in dogs with naturally occurring solid tumors.

upsert.title: Radiation and histotripsy for solid tumors in dogs and cats
upsert.center: UT Southwestern Veterinary Research and Oncology Clinic (VROC)
upsert.notes: Current VROC treatment protocol combining radiation therapy with high-intensity focused ultrasound/histotripsy for naturally occurring tumors; contact VROC for tumor-specific eligibility.

upsert.title: Calreticulin nanoparticles and HIFU immunotherapy with or without anti-PD-L1 for canine melanoma
upsert.center: UT Southwestern Veterinary Research and Oncology Clinic (VROC)
upsert.notes: Evaluates CRT-nanoparticle immunotherapy combined with HIFU, with or without anti-PD-L1, in dogs with advanced naturally occurring melanoma.

upsert.title: Intratumoral versus intravenous carboplatin with or without HIFU for canine melanoma
upsert.center: UT Southwestern Veterinary Research and Oncology Clinic (VROC)
upsert.notes: Treatment study comparing intratumoral nanoparticle/microparticle carboplatin with intravenous carboplatin, with or without HIFU enhancement.

upsert.title: Compassionate-use protocol for advanced non-resectable tumors
upsert.center: UT Southwestern Veterinary Research and Oncology Clinic (VROC)
upsert.notes: Prospective single-arm compassionate-use protocol using investigational therapy, chemotherapy, immunotherapy and combination approaches for dogs and cats with advanced non-resectable tumors. Individual treatment and eligibility are determined by VROC.

upsert.title: Experimental EGFR/HER2 tumor vaccine for canine osteosarcoma, hemangiosarcoma and transitional cell carcinoma
upsert.status: Currently enrolling at selected MedVet hospitals
upsert.funding: Vaccine is provided at no charge; hospital visits, diagnostics and vaccine administration are owner-paid because the study is not fully funded.
upsert.notes: USDA-regulated study. MedVet currently lists Salt Lake City as enrolling; Cincinnati and Cleveland are limited to established patients; Pittsburgh is limited to Pennsylvania residents; Chicago enrollment is paused. Appropriate standard-of-care treatment is required; vaccine-alone intent is not accepted.
